# ui::AnimatedImage

Header: `winui/render/Bitmap.hpp`.

An animated picture: a decoded animated GIF. The frames are already composited, each the whole picture as it should look at that point (the GIF's frame offsets, disposal and transparency applied), so a player only ever shows one of them.

A frame delay under 20 ms is shown for 100 ms, because tools write 0 or 1 hundredths and expect browsers to play it at 10 fps. [`loop_count`](#loop_count) is how many times the whole sequence plays, as the GIF's loop block says: 1 when it has none, 0 for forever.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::AnimatedImage spinner = ui::AnimatedImage::read("spinner.gif");
spinner.auto_play = false; // show the first frame until play() is called
window.set_content(ui::Image{.source = std::move(spinner)});
```

## frames

```cpp
std::vector<Bitmap> frames
```

Fully composited frames, all the same size.

## delays

```cpp
std::vector<Duration> delays
```

Display time of each frame; one per frame.

## loop_count

```cpp
int loop_count = 0
```

Plays of the whole sequence; 0 loops forever.

## auto_play

```cpp
bool auto_play = true
```

Whether an [Image](../controls/image.md#uiimage) starts playing this the moment it is given it. Off, the first frame shows until something calls play().

## empty

```cpp
bool empty() const
```

True with no frames, or an empty first frame.

## animated

```cpp
bool animated() const
```

True with more than one frame.

## width

```cpp
int width() const
```

The first frame's width in pixels; 0 with no frames.

## height

```cpp
int height() const
```

The first frame's height in pixels; 0 with no frames.

## decode

```cpp
static AnimatedImage decode(std::span<const std::uint8_t> data)
```

Every frame of an animated GIF on every platform; any other format [Bitmap::decode()](bitmap.md#decode) reads comes back as its one frame. Throws std::runtime_error if it can't be decoded.

## read

```cpp
static AnimatedImage read(const std::filesystem::path& path)
```

[decode()](#decode) of the file at `path`.
